newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO VIEW-Rate fears to hold back HK property issues.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW-Rate fears to hold back HK property issues.

text.p: Donny Kwok
Initial public offerings in Hong Kong's property sector could face a tough time in coming months as investors refocus on interest rate concerns, analysts said.

A warning of what they may face was given last week by Great Eagle Holdings Ltd, which shelved plans to spin off its office and commercial property arm Tai Shan Properties Ltd because of investors' cool stance towards property stocks.

"The market is expected to take a cautious view on property-related IPOs due to concern about an interest rate hike and following the dropping of Great Eagle's plan," said Kinson Au, senior analyst at PW Asia Brokerage said.
Great Eagle blamed fears of higher interest rates in the United States for the aborted plan.
Analysts said concerns about Tai Shan's growth prospects due to expectations of oversupply in the Grade A office market in coming years had made the issue unexciting.
Tai Shan's property portfolio was mainly Grade A office.

"It implies that many investors are cautious on the office property sector. If a candidate has a more diversified portfolio, including Grade B office space or even residential property, it will be look on more favourably," said Pamela Lam, an analyst at Pacific Challenge Securities.
Analysts said issues related to the Chinese market would also be well received.
Shares of Shenzhen municipal government backed property concern Shum Yip Holdings Co Ltd ended Friday on debut at HK$4.525 ($0.58), up 144.6 percent from the issue price of HK$1.85.
Analysts said hope of future asset injection and its strong ties with its Chinese parent had led to a success in its IPO and further boosted sentiment towards the stock on debut.

The Hong Kong public offering portion of Shum Yip's IPO was 438 times subscribed. Shum Yip engages in property development and investment in China's Shenzhen across the border from Hong Kong. It also provides transportation services in China and between Hong Kong and China.
However, property redeveloper Soundwill Holdings Ltd may have a tougher time, analysts said.

Soundwill, which specialises in redevelopment of sites in urban areas, is expected to raise HK$600 million to HK$795 million in an IPO to fund property investment and redevelopment projects in Hong Kong, market sources said.

"The risk in the business is relatively high and investors are seen worrying on the adequacy of its land bank for redevelopment," said Dennis Leung, property analyst at Dharmala Securities. "Investors may tend to buy some low risk stocks."
But outside of the property sector, analysts said demand for IPOs remained intact.

"Smaller issues, which attract mainly short-term investors, and China concepts, which are in great demand in the market, are expected to gain good support from the market despite the interest rate concerns," said Patrick Chia, research manager at China Everbright Research.
Expressway developer and operator Shenzhen Expressway Co Ltd offered 650 million H-shares at HK$2.00 to HK$2.20 each in a flotation. The subscription period for its IPO closed on Friday.
Beijing Datang Power Generation Co Ltd is expected to raise US$380 million in a 1.244 billion H-share in a dual listing in Hong Kong and London, sources said.
It is expected to launch its IPO on March 11.
Hong Kong-based knitted fabrics manufacturer Kwong Hing International Holdings Ltd said last week it was offering 45 million shares at HK$1.20 each in a Hong Kong public offering.
Its IPO will close on Wednesday.
